title: Clinical outcome in upper gastrointestinal bleeding complicating low‐dose aspirin and antithrombotic drugs

sections.abstract: <jats:sec><jats:title>Summary</jats:title></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Background</jats:title><jats:p>The current risk stratification systems in upper gastrointestinal bleeding do not correct for the intake of low‐dose aspirin and other antithrombotic drugs.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Aim</jats:title><jats:p>To test the Blatchford scores in evaluating the clinical outcome in bleeders using these drugs.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Methods</jats:title><jats:p>We calculated the Blatchford scores in 510 bleeders, including 123 on low‐dose aspirin, 44 on other antithrombotic drugs, and 68 on non‐steroidal anti‐inflammatory drugs.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Results</jats:title><jats:p>The median clinical scores distributed according to aetiological risk factors were as follows: no risk factors, 5; non‐steroidal anti‐inflammatory drugs, 8; aspirin, 7; other antithrombotics, 6; excess alcohol, 4; multiple risk factors, 7; (<jats:italic>P</jats:italic> = 0.003, Kruskal–Wallis test). Scores correlated positively with the duration of admission in the entire group (<jats:italic>r</jats:italic><jats:sub>s</jats:sub> = 0.285; <jats:italic>P</jats:italic> < 0.001) and in those taking aspirin and antithrombotics (<jats:italic>r</jats:italic><jats:sub>s</jats:sub> = 0.211; <jats:italic>P</jats:italic> = 0.029). The median scores in patients requiring the blood transfusion were 10 in the entire group and 11 in users of aspirin or antithrombotics, compared with 3 and 4, respectively, in those not transfused (<jats:italic>P</jats:italic> < 0.001).</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title><jats:p>The Blatchford scores are significantly elevated in users of non‐steroidal anti‐inflammatory drugs, low‐dose aspirin, and other antithrombotic drugs. They correlate positively with the duration of admission and the need for blood transfusion.</jats:p></jats:sec>
